video.title: Facebook Founder Mark Zuckerberg Commencement Address | Harvard Commencement 2017

motivational.video_read: Mark Zuckerberg's 2017 Harvard commencement address, delivered live with applause throughout — there is no cold-open montage, the speech starts at line 1. The material that works on a 2am viewer is not the civic 'purpose for everyone' thesis but three pockets of personal, identity-level material: the innovation run in the middle (ideas don't come out fully formed, the Eureka lie, being misunderstood, feeling like an impostor at 22), the 'they're not — you will' turn after the Facebook founding story, and the undocumented student story near the close. The rest is graduation-ceremony inspiration aimed at a graduating class, not at the person scrolling alone.

near_misses.why_not: The second landing of the student story ('if a high school senior who doesn't know what the future holds can do his part, we owe it to the world') needs the story before it — 'I can't even say his name' dangles for a stranger, and the combined run exceeds a reel-sized minute.
A list of generational projects (climate, curing disease, online voting) — inspiring at a graduation, but the viewer can pick up nothing about themselves from it.
Rowling's twelve rejections and Beyoncé's hundreds of songs are other people's résumés; 'the greatest successes come from the freedom to fail' is the only takeaway and it arrives generic.
An honest argument about luck, loans and safety nets, but it is policy aimed at the system — it leaves the broke viewer holding the problem rather than something to stand on.
The janitor-at-NASA story and the 'create a world where everyone has purpose' thesis are warm and famous, but they read as civic mission for graduates — the viewer nods instead of replaying.
The closing prayer and 'may your life be a blessing' is a gentle outro — comfort placed without any evidence or turn before it.

skipped.what: live intro, thanks, and joke anecdotes (inside-out T-shirt, Facemash, meeting Priscilla) — charming, not motivation
great-projects-of-past-generations build-up into the dam setup
transition recaps of the three-part speech structure
UBI, child care, charity and the after-school teaching story — policy and gratitude, no identity hit
global community vs nationalism — the 'struggle of our time' passage is political, not personal
community examples (Agnes, Kayla, David) and 'change starts local' — profile of others, no takeaway

clips.title: "I wondered if I was just wrong — an impostor, a 22-year-old kid who had no idea how things actually worked"
clips.description: Zuckerberg tells the story of his hardest time leading Facebook: he never explained the mission, nearly everyone wanted to sell, the management team left, and he felt alone and at fault. The payoff reframes the doubt — years later he understands that is exactly how things fall apart without a higher purpose, so it is up to all of us to create one.

Extended the end past the proposed stop at 'higher purpose' to 'moving forward together' so the reframe actually lands instead of ending on the setup clause.

clips.title: Let me tell you a secret: no one knows what they're doing when they begin — and the Eureka moment is a lie
clips.description: Zuckerberg dismantles the myth that ideas arrive fully formed: no one knows what they're doing when they start, and the 'single Eureka moment' is a dangerous lie that makes people feel inadequate and stops them from ever beginning. The clip builds from the secret to the lie, and lands on why it prevents good ideas from ever getting started.

clips.title: The idea of a single Eureka moment is a dangerous lie
clips.description: A flat, devastating correction to anyone waiting for their big moment: "movies and pop culture just get this all wrong — the idea of a single Eureka moment is a dangerous lie." It names why they feel inadequate and what that lie costs: it stops people with good ideas from ever getting started in the first place.

clips.title: Be prepared to be misunderstood
clips.description: A complete standalone thought: anyone taking on a big vision will be called crazy, blamed, and criticized — and 'that can't stop us from getting started.' The rhetorical close 'so what are we waiting for' turns the price of criticism into a call to action.

clips.title: He has every reason to be cynical — and he wasn't even thinking of himself
clips.description: A graduation speech tells the story of an undocumented student who, offered any birthday gift, asks for a book on social justice. The payoff — he has every reason to feel sorry for himself and wasn't — quietly reframes the viewer's own complaints.
clips.boundary_note: Kept the finder's span; moved the start past 'Club' (tail of the previous sentence about the Boys and Girls Club) so the clip opens cleanly on 'one day after class', and stopped at the story's landing line before the speech shifts to a new beat at L0227.

segments.text: one day after class I was talking to my students about going to college and one of my top students raised his hand and said that he wasn't sure he could go to college because he's undocumented Ed he wasn't sure if they'd take him last year I took him out to breakfast for his birthday and I wanted to get him a gift so I asked him what he wanted and he just started talking about struggles that he saw other students in his class facing and finally said you know I'd really just like a book on social justice I was blown away here is a young guy who has every reason to be cynical he wasn't sure if the country he calls home the only one he's known was going to deny him his dream of going to college but he wasn't feeling sorry for himself he wasn't even thinking of himself he has a greater sense of purpose and he's going to bring people along with him

clips.title: You're sure someone else is going to do it — but they're not. You will.
clips.description: The Facebook dorm story builds to the identity handover: a change in the world so clear you assume one of the big companies will do it — 'but they're not, you will.' The clip lands on that line and stops before the next thought begins.
clips.boundary_note: Kept the proposal as-is: it opens on the start of the dorm story (a monologue with no question to recover) and ends exactly on the landing 'you will', before 'it's not enough to have that purpose yourself' opens a new thought.

segments.start_words: I remember that night I launched Facebook
segments.text: I remember that night I launched Facebook from that little dorm in Kirkland house I went to noes with my friend KX and I remember telling him clearly that I was excited to help connect the Harvard Community but one day someone would connect the whole world the thing is it never even occurred to me that that someone might be us we were just college kids we didn't know anything about that there were all these great big technology companies with all these resources and I just assumed one of them would do it but this idea was so clear to us that all people want to connect so we just kept working on it day after day after day and I know that a lot of you are going to have your own stories just like this a change in the world that seems so clear that you are sure someone else is going to do it but they're not you will
